title: FEP-guided analogue selection (c-Met series)
context: You have a congeneric series against c-Met and a current lead (the reference ligand). Before committing synthesis you want relative binding free energies (ΔΔG vs the reference) to decide which analogues genuinely improve potency. More-negative ΔΔG = tighter binding than the lead; positive = weaker. Five analogues are shown.
decision_required: Run RBFE/FEP on the series, then recommend which analogues to advance (those meaningfully tighter-binding than the lead) and which single analogue to deprioritize (clearly weaker). Finish with a DECISION block: advance: <labels> / deprioritize: <labels> / primary_liability: <name>.

L5.note: weakest binder (+2.97 kcal/mol vs lead) — clear drop

source: Experimental ΔΔG from the N1 rbfe_benchmark (Merck/Schindler FEP, MIT). Advance = ΔΔG ≤ -1 (meaningfully tighter); drop = ΔΔG ≥ +2 (clearly weaker). Live variant grades the FEP run's ranking via rbfe_scorer.

title: FEP-guided analogue selection (SHP2 series)
